name: Vaporwave
aliases: A E S T H E T I C
plain: Pink and teal computer dream with old statues and palm trees
people_say: A E S T H E T I C text
origin: Online music scenes on Bandcamp, SoundCloud and Turntable.fm, 2010 to 2011 [S1][S4]
defining: Soft pink, lavender, cyan and peach over deep violet or navy, with neon sunsets and faded gradients [S1][S3]
Classical busts, palm trees, checker floors, perspective grids and floating old-computer windows [S1][S3][S4]
Bold capitals in full-width or stretched letters, sometimes WordArt-like; Adobe's 2021 revival adds pixel and extruded lettering [S1][S2][S4]
VHS grain, screensaver graphics and slow, detached looping drift [S1][S3]
Square corners: radius 0 to 0.25rem [S3]
fits: Music releases, game menus, digital art portfolios and nostalgic campaign pages
goes_wrong: Becomes a clip-art pile of busts and decorative Japanese text with no idea behind it; critics call that use techno-orientalism [S5]
accessibility: Pastel text on gradient skies often falls below 4.5:1, so put copy on solid dark panels; full-width letters can be read out one by one, so give the real words as an accessible name; stop VHS loops under reduced motion

sources.supports: Origin around 2010 to 2011 on online music platforms; pink and turquoise palette; statues, palms, WordArt, full-width type, VHS grain; Floral Shoppe cover
Adobe Stock's Vintage Vaporwave trend: neon and candy pastels, pixel and extruded lettering, grids, stickers and pop-ups
Palette, motifs (busts, grids, floating windows), slow drifting motion, radius 0 to 0.25rem, fit for music, gaming and art
Dates (Eccojams 2010, term in October 2011, Floral Shoppe December 2011); Windows 95 imagery, statues, full-width lettering
Retro-Japanese type criticised as techno-orientalism; Hiroshi Nagai city-pop art as a visual blueprint

examples.name: Floral Shoppe album cover (Macintosh Plus, 2011)
examples.what: Pixel graphics, a disembodied Greek bust, Japanese lettering and sickly pink

name: Synthwave
plain: Glowing pink grid road racing toward a striped sunset at night
origin: Online electronic music scenes, mid to late 2000s; the Outrun name comes from Sega's 1986 racing game [S1][S2]
defining: Midnight navy and black grounds with electric magenta, cyan, violet and sunset orange, plus chrome white highlights [S1]
Wireframe floor grid in deep perspective meeting a low neon horizon and a sun disc [S1]
Italic chrome or techno display titles; small text in a condensed sans or mono [S1]
Glowing lines and text, VHS tracking artifacts; radius 0.25 to 1rem [S1][S2]
Motion: the grid rolls toward the viewer and neon pulses [S1]
fits: Music players, game launchers, streaming, automotive and nightlife promos
goes_wrong: Glow on every element turns text into blurry halos and the page into a poster with no hierarchy
accessibility: Glow softens edges: keep body text solid and unglowed at 4.5:1 on the dark ground, keep glow for headings, and stop grid motion under reduced motion

sources.supports: Origin as a later internet-era reconstruction, Outrun naming, palette, grid and sun motifs, type, motion, radius and fit
Mid to late 2000s French house origins; VHS artifacts, magenta neon and gridlines; Drive (2011) brought it mainstream; Out Run name

name: Cyberpunk (neon noir)
plain: Dark rainy city screens with sharp neon signs and glitchy readouts
origin: Early 1980s science fiction; Syd Mead's neon-lit Los Angeles for Blade Runner (1982) set the look [S1][S2]
defining: Near-black and dirty blue-gray grounds with cyan, magenta, acid green and warning red accents [S1]
Clipped-corner panels, angled brackets, segmented bars and cable-like lines [S1][S3]
Condensed technical sans with monospace data text [S1]
Scanlines, RGB split and brief flicker tied to loading or system events [S1]
Dense, layered data panels with radius 0 to 0.25rem [S1]
fits: Game HUDs and menus, security and developer tools, nightlife and sci-fi launches
goes_wrong: Decoration in the same neon as live data, so people cannot tell controls from ornament; a cut-corner tag can look like a button [S3]
accessibility: Check every neon on black for 4.5:1 text and 3:1 edges, keep flashes under 3 per second, give decoration a dimmer color than data, and turn off glitch under reduced motion

sources.supports: Term origins (Bethke, Gibson 1984), palette, type, glitch motifs, clipped panels, motion, density and radius
Frelik (Routledge, 2022): Syd Mead's neon-lit Blade Runner city shaped later sci-fi visuals
Cyberpunk 2077 UI critique: decorative tech styling in one red blends with functional info; cut-corner tag reads as a button; chromatic aberration

examples.what: Red and yellow HUD with cut-corner tags, cable-line decoration and optional chromatic aberration

name: Solarpunk
plain: Sunny green future with plants, solar panels and curvy shapes
origin: Named in a 2008 blog post reacting to steampunk; grew on Tumblr, Medium and forums in the 2010s [S1][S2]
defining: Leaf and algae greens, terracotta, solar blue, warm yellow, soil tones and pale concrete in daylight [S2]
Curving Art Nouveau lines with vines, leaves and floral motifs [S1]
Rooftop gardens, solar greenhouses, geodesic domes and community infrastructure as imagery [S1][S2]
Humanist sans with warm editorial serif accents; radius 0.75 to 1.5rem [S2]
Gentle cycles: plants that grow, energy and water that flow [S2]
fits: Climate and energy apps, community tools, sustainability reports, civic projects
goes_wrong: Turns into stock leaf icons on an ordinary corporate page, losing the hopeful, community-made feel
accessibility: Leaf greens and sage on cream often fall below 4.5:1, so darken greens for text; pair color with labels in energy charts for color-blind users

sources.supports: ACMI: 2008 term on Republic of the Bees, Art Nouveau curves, vines and florals, Ghibli and Fuller influences, screen examples

name: Corporate Memphis

defining: Flat vector people with long limbs, small heads and simplified faces, always in motion [S1][S2]

name: Kawaii

name: Glitch art
plain: Broken screen look: split colors, torn stripes and blocky pixels
origin: Digital practice named in the late 1990s and 2000s; Oslo symposium 2002, GLI.TC/H Chicago 2010 [S1][S3]
defining: Red, green and blue channels shifted apart [S2]
Torn horizontal bands, compression blocks, pixel sorting and datamosh smears [S1][S2]
Dark or neutral ground with electric error colors and blown signal white [S2]
Distortion only on a decorative copy or large heading, with intact text underneath [S2]
Brief error bursts on transitions that settle back to stable; radius 0 to 0.25rem [S2]
fits: Music and film promos, security and tech launches, error and loading moments in games
goes_wrong: People read the intended corruption as a real bug, or the effect covers content they need
accessibility: Keep flashes under 3 per second, run effects once instead of looping, honour reduced motion, and keep a clean text copy for screen readers
